title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(阿部倫之研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III(Abe Noriyuki)
educationalGoal: Based on the concrete knowledge of fundamental technology, students acquire problem-solving skills related to computer & information engineering. Students are also given opportunities to experience R&D activities related to concrete information technology and systems. Through this process, students cultivate advanced abilities in the areas of problem setting, production process development, information gathering, communications, problem-solving in regional orientation, and making objective evaluations.
advice: In this project, students learn R&D methods in the social computing field using social networking services such as Twitter and Facebook. Research subjects focused on in this project are as follows: 1. Clustering of active users based on the retweet patterns of the disaster information on Twitter. 2. User recommendation systems that use activity logs in tweet postings. 3. The study of a predictive evaluation method for market conditions using sentiment polarity on reactive tweets.
books: Textbooks: None Reference books: None Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: In this course, the laboratory presents the main theme and the students consider various subthemes. In the laboratory, regular seminars are held every week, and regular presentations are held every month. It is desirable for students to have acquired basic programming skills using Java language.

activityGoals.body: Be able to set one-year achievement goals in relation to your chosen research.
Be able to set a specific production approach based on your set research concept.
Be able to use your acquired information engineering expertise to advance your design and analysis efforts.
Be able to cope with various problems that occur during the design and analysis process.
Be able to technically describe what you have accomplished in a convincing manner.

lessons.content: Spring Semester: Progress reports and study sessions are held every week.
Summer Season: Study session for implementation. Implementation. Presentation for the interim report meeting.
Fall Semester: 15-minute progress report/month. Explore each research area.
